focus: 為已經動手的流程改變辯護
lead: 今天練的是為一個你已經先做了、才拿出來講的決定辯護：先劃清「什麼變了、什麼沒變」，再用一個關鍵數字說明你被什麼說服，最後主動說「我判斷錯的話，最先壞掉的是哪裡」。這種場合最容易犯的錯是把辯護講成道歉 —— 今天每個 speaking 段落都請先出聲講完，再看 model answer。

phrases.en: We changed how X works, and here's what stays the same.
phrases.gl: 我們改了 X 的做法，而以下這些沒有變（先安撫範圍，再談改動）
phrases.ex: We changed how the labeling queue gets fed, and here's what stays the same: the taxonomy, the audit gate, and your sign-off before anything ships.

phrases.en: The number that convinced me was…
phrases.gl: 真正說服我的那個數字是 ——（把決定的來源指向證據，而不是你的偏好）
phrases.ex: The number that convinced me was the edit rate — annotators are changing 11% of the pre-labeled boxes, not 1%, so they're clearly still looking.

phrases.gl: 這個決定我負責（承擔，但不道歉；比 “sorry for that” 專業得多）
phrases.ex: Rolling it out before the group met was my decision, and I'll own that call.

phrases.en: We ran it on a slice first.
phrases.gl: 我們先在一小塊資料上跑過（證明不是直接全量開下去）
phrases.ex: We ran it on a slice first — two weeks of urban daytime, about 40,000 frames — before we touched the main queue.

phrases.gl: 這件事不會動到的是 ——（劃出影響邊界，止住恐慌）
phrases.ex: What this doesn't change is the holdout set. That's still labeled from scratch, no model involved.

phrases.en: If I'm wrong, the first thing to break is…
phrases.gl: 如果我判斷錯，最先出問題的地方是 ——（顯示你知道自己的風險長什麼樣）
phrases.ex: If I'm wrong, the first thing to break is recall on small distant objects at night — that's where the model and the humans disagree most.

phrases.en: I'd rather be corrected now than in October.
phrases.gl: 我寧願現在被糾正，而不是十月才發現（邀請質疑，語氣不軟）
phrases.ex: So push on the audit design if you think it's thin — I'd rather be corrected now than in October.

phrases.en: We've been running it that way since June.
phrases.gl: 我們從六月就一直是這樣跑的（中文「一直」在英文要用完成式，不是現在式）
phrases.ex: We've been running the pre-label step on the urban set since June, so this isn't a new experiment.
phrases.fix: 取代 “Until now we always do like this”

phrases.en: Two things are getting mixed up here — let me separate them.
phrases.gl: 這裡有兩件事被混在一起了，我把它們拆開（比指責對方誤會安全得多）
phrases.ex: Two things are getting mixed up here — let me separate them: whether the labels are accurate, and whether they're biased toward the model.
phrases.fix: 取代 “I think you misunderstand my meaning”

setup: Setup. You called this review to defend a change you already rolled out: the labeling vendor no longer draws boxes from scratch. The current detector pre-labels every frame, and the annotators only correct and confirm. Cost per frame went from about 42 cents to 16, weekly throughput went from roughly 60,000 frames to 210,000, and the 1.4-million-frame backlog finally started shrinking. Grace, who runs labeling ops, thinks the annotators are quietly rubber-stamping whatever the model hands them. Rachel, on the data science side, says training the next model on labels the current one produced will bake in its own blind spots, and Vincent wants to know whether the saving is real or just moved onto your team.

prompts.q: Grace: “Walk us through what actually changed — and why this landed on my team before it came to this room.”
prompts.frame: Name the change in one line → what stays the same → the pilot and the number that convinced you → own the process mistake without apologizing for the decision → hand her one control.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 50 秒）。第一句講「變了什麼」，第二句馬上講「什麼沒變」，不要先鋪陳背景。
prompts.model: “Sure. We changed how the queue gets fed: the detector pre-labels every frame, and your annotators correct instead of drawing from scratch. And here's what stays the same — the taxonomy, the audit gate, the 5% stratified sample, and your sign-off before any batch is released. Nobody's job changed shape except the first thirty seconds of each frame. We ran it on a slice first, two weeks of urban daytime, about forty thousand frames. The number that convinced me was the edit rate: annotators are changing 11% of the pre-labeled boxes. If they were rubber-stamping, that number would be near zero. On the process — you're right, this should have come to the group before it went to your queue, and I'll own that call. What I'd like from you is the audit design. If 5% is too thin to catch drift, tell me what it needs to be and I'll fund it.”

prompts.q: Rachel: “My problem isn't the cost, it's the loop. You're training the next model on labels the current model wrote. It'll learn to agree with itself.”
prompts.frame: Agree that the risk is real → separate the two things being conflated → give the clean-holdout protection with numbers → say what you'd watch and what you'd do → invite her to set the threshold.
prompts.say: 出聲練「承認風險但不退讓」。開場不要用 “I think maybe”，也不要用 “you misunderstand”。
prompts.model: “That risk is real and I don't want to talk you out of it. But two things are getting mixed up here — let me separate them. One is whether the labels are accurate. Two is whether they're biased toward what the model already believes. On accuracy, we re-labeled a sample from scratch and blind, and agreement came out at 96.3%. On bias, that's the one I actually worry about, and it's why the holdout is untouched — forty thousand frames, labeled from scratch, no pre-labeling ever, and that's what we evaluate on. So the loop can't hide from the eval. If I'm wrong, the first thing to break is recall on small distant objects at night, because that's exactly where the model and the humans disagree most today. So here's what I'd offer: you pick the metric and the floor. If night recall on the clean holdout drops two points, we pull pre-labeling off the night set and go back to from-scratch there. Would you rather set that at two points or one?”

prompts.q: Vincent: “Straight answer — is the saving real, or did the cost just move to your side of the house?”
prompts.frame: Answer the question first, including the part that hurts → give both sides of the ledger with numbers → say what you actually bought with it → name what you would give up if it stops being worth it.
prompts.say: 出聲講一次，控制在 35 秒。不要美化 —— 主動講出成本轉移的那一塊。
prompts.model: “Partly moved, and I'll be straight about that. Per frame, it's real: forty-two cents down to sixteen. Weekly spend is actually slightly up, because we're pushing three and a half times the volume through. On our side, the new cost is about half a headcount on auditing plus roughly two thousand a month in inference. So the honest version is: we didn't cut the labeling bill, we bought throughput at a much better rate. What that buys the program is the backlog cleared before the platform build freezes instead of two quarters after it. If the audit ever shows the quality slipping, the first thing I'd cut is the volume, not the audit — and I'd rather be corrected now than in October, so if the trade doesn't look worth it to you, say so today.”

fixes.bad: The vendor give us two feedbacks about the pre-label quality last week.
fixes.good: The vendor gave us two pieces of feedback on the pre-label quality last week.
fixes.note: Uncountable + agreement：feedback 不可數，沒有 feedbacks，要數就用 two pieces of feedback；主詞是單數第三人稱，過去的事用 gave。

fixes.bad: Maybe we can try to consider to change the labeling flow.
fixes.good: I'd like us to change the labeling flow.
fixes.note: Vague hedging：maybe + try to + consider 三層緩衝疊在一起，聽起來像你自己也不相信這個提案。想留餘地只用一層就好（I'd like / I'd suggest），而且 consider 後面要接 -ing。

fixes.bad: After the change, the cost per frame is cheap 60 percent than before.
fixes.good: After the change, the cost per frame is about 60% lower than before.
fixes.note: Comparative form：cheap 不能這樣接數字和 than，比較用 lower / cheaper by；口說時把百分比放在形容詞前面（60% lower）最清楚。

fixes.bad: If the audit will fail, we will roll back to manual labeling.
fixes.good: If the audit fails, we'll roll back to manual labeling.
fixes.note: Conditional：if 引導的條件句不用 will，用現在式；未來只出現在主句（we'll roll back）。

fixes.bad: I need to confirm with Grace first, then I can reply you the schedule.
fixes.good: I need to check with Grace first, then I can get back to you on the schedule.
fixes.note: Literal translation：中文的「確認」多半是「去問一下」，英文用 check with；confirm with 聽起來像要對方替你背書。另外 reply 不能直接接人，要 reply to you 或更口語的 get back to you。

challenge:
今天在真實會議裡用這一組句型（做到一次就算成功）：

“We changed how ___ works, and here's what stays the same: ___. The number that convinced me was ___. If I'm wrong, the first thing to break is ___.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：挑一個你「先做了、後來才對外說明」的決定，用英文走一遍。

  • 前兩句必須是「變了什麼 / 沒變什麼」，不准先講背景或先道歉
  • 中間必須出現一次 I'll own that call，而且後面不接 sorry
  • 結尾必須自己講出「我錯的話最先壞掉的是什麼」，並把一個門檻的決定權交給對方
  • 禁用：maybe we can try to consider、you misunderstand、if it will fail、reply you
check: 我有把「什麼變了」和「什麼沒變」分開講，還是只顧著解釋為什麼要改？
我承擔責任的時候，是說 I'll own that call，還是滑進連續道歉？
被質疑時我有主動說出自己的失敗訊號（first thing to break），還是等對方挖出來？
